analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction ('This wasn't my fault') about overdraft fees and alleges financial loss of £30, meeting CH-1.
analysis.summary: Customer's salary credit due 30 September arrived late. Her account went overdrawn and two £15 unarranged overdraft fees were charged (30/09 and 01/10). She asks for the £30 to be refunded. The handler found incident INC-4471, a batch delay on inbound Faster Payments on 30/09, with credits applied 01/10. This suggests the fees may have resulted from a bank system fault, which would bring FEE-2 into scope. The loss is under £100. No vulnerability indicators were noted. The customer prefers email. The complaints handler can resolve this without a specialist; the outcome and any redress are for the handler to decide.

timeline.event: Expected salary credit did not arrive; account went overdrawn; first £15 unarranged overdraft fee charged
INC-4471 batch delay on inbound Faster Payments; UOD fee £15
Delayed credits applied; second UOD fee £15
Complaint received by email and logged; incident log checked

analysis.severity_reason: Financial loss of £30, under £100, with no other High or Medium triggers (CH-6). The incident affected a batch of payments, but there is no indication in the file that it is an unresolved systemic complaint issue.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None identified; continue contact by email as preferred.

analysis.routing_reason: No ESC-1 trigger applies: this is a fee complaint with no fraud, lending, vulnerability referral or need for technical investigation, because the incident is already recorded as INC-4471. The complaints handler can resolve it.

policy_citations.quote: Low: financial loss under £100 or a service issue with no loss.

Where a fee was charged because of a bank error (for example a system fault, an incorrect tariff or a payment the bank failed to process on time), the fee must be refunded in full, together with any interest charged on it, plus a goodwill payment in line with policy RED.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: INC-4471 indicates the fees may stem from a bank processing delay. The handler should assess whether FEE-2 applies.
The disputed fees are within the scope of the fees policy.

policy_citations.quote: Complaints handlers resolve complaints themselves unless one of the following applies
policy_citations.how_it_applies: None of the escalation triggers apply.

evidence.quote: you charged me two unarranged overdraft fees of £15 each
INC-4471 batch delay on inbound Faster Payments 30/09, credits applied 01/10
Two UOD fees £15 on 30/09 and 01/10 confirmed
No vulnerability indicators, cust says she's fine just annoyed

handover.complaint_summary: Salary credit delayed by a bank Faster Payments batch delay (INC-4471) caused the account to go overdrawn, and two £15 unarranged overdraft fees were charged. The customer wants them refunded.
actions_taken: Incident log checked; INC-4471 identified and fees confirmed
handover.vulnerability_assessment: No indicators found. The customer said she was 'fine just annoyed'. The case does not record that she was formally asked about support needs.
open_questions: Was the salary payment received by the bank on 30/09 and delayed by INC-4471, confirming the fees resulted from bank error?
Was any interest charged on the overdrawn balance or the fees?

other_gaps: Whether any overdraft interest was charged is not recorded
Whether the customer was explicitly asked about support needs is not recorded
analysis.suggested_next_step: The handler should confirm against INC-4471 and the statement that the salary payment was caught in the batch delay. They should then decide the outcome and any redress under FEE-2/RED, and respond by email. This may be suitable for summary resolution if agreed by the third business day.
